L1@P0: FUNGIZONE - amphotericin b injection, powder, lyophilized, for solution
L2@P0: E.R. Squibb & Sons, L.L.C.
L3@P0: WARNING
L4@P0: This drug should be used primarily for treatment of patients with progressive and potentially life-threatening fungal
L5@P0: infections; it should not be used to treat noninvasive forms of fungal disease such as oral thrush, vaginal candidiasis, and
L6@P0: esophageal candidiasis in patients with normal neutrophil counts.
L7@P0: FUNGIZONE Intravenous should not be given at doses greater than 1.5 mg/kg. EXERCISE CAUTION to prevent
L8@P0: inadvertent overdosage, which can result in potentially fatal cardiac or cardiopulmonary arrest (see WARNINGS,
L9@P0: OVERDOSAGE, and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Verify the product name and dosage pre-administration,
L10@P0: especially if dose exceeds 1.5 mg/kg.
L11@P0: DESCRIPTION
L12@P0: FUNGIZONE Intravenous (Amphotericin B for Injection) contains amphotericin B, an antifungal polyene
L13@P0: antibiotic obtained from a strain of Streptomyces nodosus. Amphotericin B is designated chemically as [1R-
L14@P0: (1R*,3S*,5R*,6R*,9R*,11R*,15S*,16R*,17R*,18S*,19E,21E,23E,25E,27E,29E,31E,33R*,35S*,36R*,37S*)]-33-
L15@P0: [(3-Amino-3,6-dideoxy-β-D-mannopyranosyl)-oxy]-1,3,5,6,9,11,17,37-octahydroxy-15,16,18-trimethyl-13-oxo-14,39-
L16@P0: dioxabicyclo[33.3.1]nonatriaconta-19,21,23,25,27,29,31-heptaene-36-carboxylic acid. Structural formula:
L17@P0: C47H73NO17 MW 924.09
L18@P0: Each vial contains a sterile, nonpyrogenic, lyophilized cake (which may partially reduce to powder following manufacture) providing
L19@P0: 50 mg amphotericin B and 41 mg sodium desoxycholate with 20.2 mg sodium phosphate as a buffer. Crystalline amphotericin B is
L20@P0: insoluble in water; therefore, the antibiotic is solubilized by the addition of sodium desoxycholate to form a mixture which provides a
L21@P0: colloidal dispersion for intravenous infusion following reconstitution.
L22@P0: At the time of manufacture the air in the vial is replaced by nitrogen.
L23@P0: CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY
L24@P0: Microbiology
L25@P0: Amphotericin B shows a high order of in vitro activity against many species of fungi. Histoplasma capsulatum, Coccidioides immitis,
L26@P0: Candida species, Blastomyces dermatitidis, Rhodotorula, Cryptococcus neoformans, Sporothrix schenckii, Mucor mucedo, and
L27@P0: Aspergillus fumigatus are all inhibited by concentrations of amphotericin B ranging from 0.03 to 1.0 mcg/mL in vitro. While Candida
L28@P0: albicans is generally quite susceptible to amphotericin B, non-albicans species may be less susceptible. Pseudallescheria boydii and
L29@P0: Fusarium sp. are often resistant to amphotericin B. The antibiotic is without effect on bacteria, rickettsiae, and viruses.
L30@P0: Susceptibility Testing
L31@P0: Standardized techniques for susceptibility testing for antifungal agents have not been established and results of susceptibility studies
L32@P0: have not been correlated with clinical outcomes.
L33@P0: Pharmacokinetics
L34@P0: Amphotericin B is fungistatic or fungicidal depending on the concentration obtained in body fluids and the susceptibility of
L35@P0: the fungus. The drug acts by binding to sterols in the cell membrane of susceptible fungi with a resultant change in membrane
L36@P0: permeability allowing leakage of intracellular components. Mammalian cell membranes also contain sterols and it has been suggested
L37@P0: that the damage to human cells and fungal cells may share common mechanisms.
L38@P0: An initial intravenous infusion of 1 to 5 mg of amphotericin B per day, gradually increased to 0.4 to 0.6 mg/kg daily, produces
L39@P0: peak plasma concentrations ranging from approximately 0.5 to 2 mcg/mL. Following a rapid initial fall, plasma concentrations
L40@P0: plateau at about 0.5 mcg/mL. An elimination half-life of approximately 15 days follows an initial plasma half-life of about 24 hours.
L41@P0: Amphotericin B circulating in plasma is highly bound (>90%) to plasma proteins and is poorly dialyzable. Approximately two thirds
L42@P0: of concurrent plasma concentrations have been detected in fluids from inflamed pleura, peritoneum, synovium, and aqueous humor.
L43@P0: Concentrations in the cerebrospinal fluid seldom exceed 2.5% of those in the plasma. Little amphotericin B penetrates into vitreous
L44@P0: humor or normal amniotic fluid. Complete details of tissue distribution are not known.
L45@P0: Amphotericin B is excreted very slowly (over weeks to months) by the kidneys with 2 to 5% of a given dose being excreted in the
L46@P0-1: biologically active form. Details of possible metabolic pathways are not known. After treatment is discontinued, the drug can bepage 2 of 6
L47@P1: detected in the urine for at least 7 weeks due to the slow disappearance of the drug. The cumulative urinary output over a 7-day period
L48@P1: amounts to approximately 40% of the amount of drug infused.
L49@P1: INDICATIONS AND USAGE
L50@P1: FUNGIZONE Intravenous (Amphotericin B for Injection, USP) should be administered primarily to patients with progressive,
L51@P1: potentially life-threatening fungal infections. This potent drug should not be used to treat noninvasive fungal infections, such as oral
L52@P1: thrush, vaginal candidiasis, and esophageal candidiasis in patients with normal neutrophil counts.
L53@P1: FUNGIZONE Intravenous is specifically intended to treat potentially life-threatening fungal infections: aspergillosis, cryptococcosis
L54@P1: (torulosis), North American blastomycosis, systemic candidiasis, coccidioido-mycosis, histoplasmosis, zygomycosis including
L55@P1: mucormycosis due to susceptible species of the genera Absidia, Mucor, and Rhizopus, and infections due to related susceptible species
L56@P1: of Conidiobolus and Basidiobolus, and sporotrichosis.
L57@P1: Amphotericin B may be useful in the treatment of American mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, but it is not the drug of choice as primary
L58@P1: therapy.
L59@P1: CONTRAINDICATIONS
L60@P1: This product is contraindicated in those patients who have shown hypersensitivity to amphotericin B or any other component in
L61@P1: the formulation unless, in the opinion of the physician, the condition requiring treatment is life-threatening and amenable only to
L62@P1: amphotericin B therapy.
L63@P1: WARNINGS
L64@P1: Amphotericin B is frequently the only effective treatment available for potentially life-threatening fungal disease. In each case, its
L65@P1: possible life-saving benefit must be balanced against its untoward and dangerous side effects.
L66@P1: EXERCISE CAUTION to prevent inadvertent FUNGIZONE Intravenous overdose, which can result in potentially fatal cardiac or
L67@P1: cardiorespiratory arrest. Verify the product name and dosage pre-administration, especially if dose prescribed exceeds 1.5 mg/kg
L68@P1: (see OVERDOSAGE and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
L69@P1: PRECAUTIONS
L70@P1: General
L71@P1: Amphotericin B should be administered intravenously under close clinical observation by medically trained personnel. It should be
L72@P1: reserved for treatment of patients with progressive, potentially life-threatening fungal infections due to susceptible organisms (see
L73@P1: INDICATIONS AND USAGE).
L74@P1: Acute reactions including fever, shaking chills, hypotension, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, headache, and tachypnea are common 1 to
L75@P1: 3 hours after starting an intravenous infusion. These reactions are usually more severe with the first few doses of amphotericin B and
L76@P1: usually diminish with subsequent doses.
L77@P1: Rapid intravenous infusion has been associated with hypotension, hypokalemia, arrhythmias, and shock and should, therefore, be
L78@P1: avoided (see DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
L79@P1: Amphotericin B should be used with care in patients with reduced renal function; frequent monitoring of renal function is
L80@P1: recommended (see PRECAUTIONS: Laboratory Tests and ADVERSE REACTIONS). In some patients hydration and sodium
L81@P1: repletion prior to amphotericin B administration may reduce the risk of developing nephrotoxicity. Supplemental alkali medication
L82@P1: may decrease renal tubular acidosis complications.
L83@P1: Since acute pulmonary reactions have been reported in patients given amphotericin B during or shortly after leukocyte transfusions, it
L84@P1: is advisable to temporarily separate these infusions as far as possible and to monitor pulmonary function (see PRECAUTIONS: Drug
L85@P1: Interactions).
L86@P1: Leukoencephalopathy has been reported following use of amphotericin B. Literature reports have suggested that total body irradiation
L87@P1: may be a predisposition.
L88@P1: Whenever medication is interrupted for a period longer than 7 days, therapy should be resumed by starting with the lowest dosage
L89@P1: level, e.g., 0.25 mg/kg of body weight, and increased gradually as outlined under DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION.
L90@P1: Laboratory Tests
L91@P1: Renal function should be monitored frequently during amphotericin B therapy (see ADVERSE REACTIONS). It is also advisable to
L92@P1: monitor on a regular basis liver function, serum electrolytes (particularly magnesium and potassium), blood counts, and hemoglobin
L93@P1: concentrations. Laboratory test results should be used as a guide to subsequent dosage adjustments.
L94@P1: Drug Interactions
L95@P1: When administered concurrently, the following drugs may interact with amphotericin B:
L96@P1: Antineoplastic agents: may enhance the potential for renal toxicity, bronchospasm and hypotension. Antineoplastic agents (e.g.,
L97@P1: nitrogen mustard, etc.) should be given concomitantly only with great caution.
L98@P1: Corticosteroids and Corticotropin (ACTH): may potentiate amphotericin B-induced hypokalemia which may predispose the patient to
L99@P1: cardiac dysfunction. Avoid concomitant use unless necessary to control side effects of amphotericin B. If used concomitantly, closely
L100@P1-2: monitor serum electrolytes and cardiac function (see ADVERSE REACTIONS).page 3 of 6
L101@P2: Digitalis glycosides: amphotericin B-induced hypokalemia may potentiate digitalis toxicity. Serum potassium levels and cardiac
L102@P2: function should be closely monitored and any deficit promptly corrected.
L103@P2: Flucytosine: while a synergistic relationship with amphotericin B has been reported, concomitant use may increase the toxicity of
L104@P2: flucytosine by possibly increasing its cellular uptake and/or impairing its renal excretion.
L105@P2: Imidazoles (e.g., ketoconazole, miconazole, clotrimazole, fluconazole, etc.): in vitro and animal studies with the combination of
L106@P2: amphotericin B and imidazoles suggest that imidazoles may induce fungal resistance to amphotericin B. Combination therapy should
L107@P2: be administered with caution, especially in immunocompromised patients.
L108@P2: Other nephrotoxic medications: agents such as aminoglycosides, cyclosporine, and pentamidine may enhance the potential for
L109@P2: drug-induced renal toxicity, and should be used concomitantly only with great caution. Intensive monitoring of renal function is
L110@P2: recommended in patients requiring any combination of nephrotoxic medications (see PRECAUTIONS: Laboratory Tests).
L111@P2: Skeletal muscle relaxants: amphotericin B-induced hypokalemia may enhance the curariform effect of skeletal muscle relaxants (e.g.,
L112@P2: tubocurarine). Serum potassium levels should be monitored and deficiencies corrected.
L113@P2: Leukocyte transfusions: acute pulmonary toxicity has been reported in patients receiving intravenous amphotericin B and leukocyte
L114@P2: transfusions (see PRECAUTIONS: General).
L115@P2: Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility
L116@P2: No long-term studies in animals have been performed to evaluate carcinogenic potential. There also have been no studies to determine
L117@P2: mutagenicity or whether this medication affects fertility in males or females.
L118@P2: Pregnancy: Teratogenic Effects, Pregnancy Category B
L119@P2: Reproduction studies in animals have revealed no evidence of harm to the fetus due to amphotericin B for injection. Systemic fungal
L120@P2: infections have been successfully treated in pregnant women with amphotericin B for injection without obvious effects to the fetus,
L121@P2: but the number of cases reported has been small. Because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response,
L122@P2: and adequate and well-controlled studies have not been conducted in pregnant women, this drug should be used during pregnancy only
L123@P2: if clearly indicated.
L124@P2: Nursing Mothers
L125@P2: It is not known whether amphotericin B is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk and considering
L126@P2: the potential toxicity of amphotericin B, it is prudent to advise a nursing mother to discontinue nursing.
L127@P2: Pediatric Use
L128@P2: Safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients have not been established through adequate and well-controlled studies. Systemic fungal
L129@P2: infections have been successfully treated in pediatric patients without reports of unusual side effects. Amphotericin B for Injection
L130@P2: when administered to pediatric patients should be limited to the smallest dose compatible with an effective therapeutic regimen.
L131@P2: ADVERSE REACTIONS
L132@P2: Although some patients may tolerate full intravenous doses of amphotericin B without difficulty, most will exhibit some intolerance,
L133@P2: often at less than the full therapeutic dose.
L134@P2: Tolerance may be improved by treatment with aspirin, antipyretics (e.g., acetaminophen), antihistamines, or antiemetics. Meperidine
L135@P2: (25 to 50 mg IV) has been shown in some patients to decrease the duration of shaking chills and fever that may accompany the
L136@P2: infusion of amphotericin B.
L137@P2: Administration of amphotericin B on alternate days may decrease anorexia and phlebitis.
L138@P2: Intravenous administration of small doses of adrenal corticosteroids just prior to or during the amphotericin B infusion may help
L139@P2: decrease febrile reactions. Dosage and duration of such corticosteroid therapy should be kept to a minimum (see PRECAUTIONS:
L140@P2: Drug Interactions).
L141@P2: Addition of heparin (1000 units per infusion), and the use of pediatric scalp-vein needle may lessen the incidence of thrombophlebitis.
L142@P2: Extravasation may cause chemical irritation.
L143@P2: The adverse reactions most commonly observed are:
L144@P2: General (body as a whole): fever (sometimes accompanied by shaking chills usually occurring within 15 to 20 minutes after initiation
L145@P2: of treatment); malaise; weight loss.
L146@P2: Cardiopulmonary: hypotension; tachypnea.
L147@P2: Gastrointestinal: anorexia; nausea; vomiting; diarrhea; dyspepsia; cramping epigastric pain.
L148@P2: Hematologic: normochromic, normocytic anemia.
L149@P2: Local: pain at the injection site with or without phlebitis or thrombophlebitis.
L150@P2: Musculoskeletal: generalized pain, including muscle and joint pains.
L151@P2: Neurologic: headache.
L152@P2: Renal: decreased renal function and renal function abnormalities including: azotemia, hypokalemia, hyposthenuria, renal tubular
L153@P2: acidosis; and nephrocalcinosis. These usually improve with interruption of therapy. However, some permanent impairment
L154@P2-3: often occurs, especially in those patients receiving large amounts (over 5 g) of amphotericin B or receiving other nephrotoxicpage 4 of 6
L155@P3: agents. In some patients hydration and sodium repletion prior to amphotericin B administration may reduce the risk of developing
L156@P3: nephrotoxicity. Supplemental alkali medication may decrease renal tubular acidosis.
L157@P3: The following adverse reactions have also been reported:
L158@P3: General (body as a whole): flushing.
L159@P3: Allergic: anaphylactoid and other allergic reactions; bronchospasm; wheezing.
L160@P3: Cardiopulmonary: cardiac arrest; shock; cardiac failure; pulmonary edema; hypersensitivity pneumonitis; arrhythmias, including
L161@P3: ventricular fibrillation; dyspnea; hypertension.
L162@P3: Dermatologic: rash, in particular maculopapular; pruritus. Skin exfoliation, toxic epidermal necrolysis, and Stevens-Johnson
L163@P3: syndrome have been reported during post-marketing surveillance.
L164@P3: Gastrointestinal: acute liver failure; hepatitis; jaundice; hemorrhagic gastroenteritis; melena.
L165@P3: Hematologic: agranulocytosis; coagulation defects; thrombocytopenia; leukopenia; eosinophilia; leukocytosis.
L166@P3: Neurologic: convulsions; hearing loss; tinnitus; transient vertigo; visual impairment; diplopia; peripheral neuropathy; encephalopathy
L167@P3: (see PRECAUTIONS); other neurologic symptoms.
L168@P3: Renal: acute renal failure; anuria; oliguria. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus has been reported during post-marketing surveillance.
L169@P3: Altered Laboratory Findings
L170@P3: Serum Electrolytes: Hypomagnesemia; hypo- and hyperkalemia; hypocalcemia.
L171@P3: Liver Function Tests: Elevations of AST, ALT, GGT, bilirubin, and alkaline phosphatase.
L172@P3: Renal Function Tests: Elevations of BUN and serum creatinine.
L173@P3: OVERDOSAGE
L174@P3: Amphotericin B overdoses can result in potentially fatal cardiac or cardiorespiratory arrest (see WARNINGS and DOSAGE
L175@P3: AND ADMINISTRATION). If an overdose is suspected, discontinue therapy and monitor the patient’s clinical status (e.g.,
L176@P3: cardiorespiratory, renal, and liver function, hematologic status, serum electrolytes) and administer supportive therapy, as required.
L177@P3: Amphotericin B is not hemodialyzable.
L178@P3: Prior to reinstituting therapy, the patient’s condition should be stabilized (including correction of electrolyte deficiencies, etc.).
L179@P3: DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION
L180@P3: **VERIFY PRODUCT NAME AND DOSAGE.**
L181@P3: CAUTION: Under no circumstances should a total daily dose of 1.5 mg/kg be exceeded. Amphotericin B overdoses can result
L182@P3: in potentially fatal cardiac or cardiorespiratory arrest (see WARNINGS and OVERDOSAGE).
L183@P3: FUNGIZONE Intravenous (Amphotericin B for Injection) should be administered by slow intravenous infusion. Intravenous infusion
L184@P3: should be given over a period of approximately 2 to 6 hours (depending on the dose) observing the usual precautions for intravenous
L185@P3: therapy (see PRECAUTIONS: General). The recommended concentration for intravenous infusion is 0.1 mg/mL (1 mg/10 mL).
L186@P3: Since patient tolerance varies greatly, the dosage of amphotericin B must be individualized and adjusted according to the patient’s
L187@P3: clinical status (e.g., site and severity of infection, etiologic agent, cardio-renal function, etc.).
L188@P3: A single intravenous test dose (1 mg in 20 mL of 5% dextrose solution) administered over 20 to 30 minutes may be preferred. The
L189@P3: patient’s temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure should be recorded every 30 minutes for 2 to 4 hours.
L190@P3: In patients with good cardio-renal function and a well tolerated test dose, therapy is usually initiated with a daily dose of 0.25 mg/
L191@P3: kg of body weight. However, in those patients having severe and rapidly progressive fungal infection, therapy may be initiated with
L192@P3: a daily dose of 0.3 mg/kg of body weight. In patients with impaired cardio-renal function or a severe reaction to the test dose,
L193@P3: therapy should be initiated with smaller daily doses (i.e., 5 to 10 mg).
L194@P3: Depending on the patient’s cardio-renal status (see PRECAUTIONS: Laboratory Tests), doses may gradually be increased by 5 to
L195@P3: 10 mg per day to final daily dosage of 0.5 to 0.7 mg/kg.
L196@P3: There are insufficient data presently available to define total dosage requirements and duration of treatment necessary for eradication
L197@P3: of specific mycoses. The optimal dose is unknown. Total daily dosage may range up to 1.0 mg/kg per day or up to 1.5 mg/kg when
L198@P3: given on alternate days.
L199@P3: Sporotrichosis: Therapy with intravenous amphotericin B for sporotrichosis has ranged up to 9 months with a total dose up to 2.5 g.
L200@P3: Aspergillosis: Aspergillosis has been treated with amphotericin B intravenously for a period up to 11 months with a total dose up to
L201@P3: 3.6 g.
L202@P3: Rhinocerebral phycomycosis: This fulminating disease generally occurs in association with diabetic ketoacidosis. It is,
L203@P3: therefore, imperative that diabetic control be restored in order for treatment with FUNGIZONE Intravenous to be successful.
L204@P3: In contradistinction, pulmonary phycomycosis, which is more common in association with hematologic malignancies, is often
L205@P3: an incidental finding at autopsy. A cumulative dose of at least 3 g of amphotericin B is recommended to treat rhinocerebral
L206@P3: phycomycosis. Although a total dose of 3 to 4 g will infrequently cause lasting renal impairment, this would seem a reasonable
L207@P3: minimum where there is clinical evidence of invasion of deep tissue. Since rhinocerebral phycomycosis usually follows a rapidly fatal
L208@P3-4: course, the therapeutic approach must necessarily be more aggressive than that used in more indolent mycoses.page 5 of 6
L209@P4: Preparation of Solutions
L210@P4: Reconstitute as follows: An initial concentrate of 5 mg amphotericin B per mL is first prepared by rapidly expressing 10 mL Sterile
L211@P4: Water for Injection, USP without a bacteriostatic agent directly into the lyophilized cake, using a sterile needle (minimum diameter:
L212@P4: 20 gauge) and syringe. Shake the vial immediately until the colloidal solution is clear. The infusion solution, providing 0.1 mg
L213@P4: amphotericin B per mL, is then obtained by further dilution (1:50) with 5% Dextrose Injection, USP of pH above 4.2. The pH of
L214@P4: each container of Dextrose Injection should be ascertained before use. Commercial Dextrose Injection usually has a pH above
L215@P4: 4.2; however, if it is below 4.2, then 1 or 2 mL of buffer should be added to the Dextrose Injection before it is used to dilute the
L216@P4: concentrated solution of amphotericin B. The recommended buffer has the following composition:
L217@P4:  Dibasic sodium phosphate (anhydrous) 1.59 g
L218@P4:  Monobasic sodium phosphate (anhydrous) 0.96 g
L219@P4:  Water for Injection, USP qs 100.0 mL
L220@P4: The buffer should be sterilized before it is added to the Dextrose Injection, either by filtration through a bacterial retentive stone, mat,
L221@P4: or membrane, or by autoclaving for 30 minutes at 15 lb pressure (121° C).
L222@P4: CAUTION: Aseptic technique must be strictly observed in all handling, since no preservative or bacteriostatic agent is present
L223@P4: in the antibiotic or in the materials used to prepare it for administration. All entries into the vial or into the diluents must be made
L224@P4: with a sterile needle. Do not reconstitute with saline solutions. The use of any diluent other than the ones recommended or the
L225@P4: presence of a bacteriostatic agent (e.g., benzyl alcohol) in the diluent may cause precipitation of the antibiotic. Do not use the
L226@P4: initial concentrate or the infusion solution if there is any evidence of precipitation or foreign matter in either one.
L227@P4: An in-line membrane filter may be used for intravenous infusion of amphotericin B; however, the mean pore diameter of the filter
L228@P4: should not be less than 1.0 micron in order to assure passage of the antibiotic dispersion.
L229@P4: HOW SUPPLIED
L230@P4: FUNGIZONE Intravenous (Amphotericin B for Injection, USP)
L231@P4: Available as single vials providing 50 mg amphotericin B as a yellow to orange lyophilized cake (which may partially reduce to
L232@P4: powder following manufacture). NDC 0003-0437-30.
L233@P4: Storage
L234@P4: Prior to reconstitution FUNGIZONE Intravenous should be stored in the refrigerator, protected against exposure to light. The
L235@P4: concentrate (5 mg amphotericin B per mL after reconstitution with 10 mL Sterile Water for Injection, USP) may be stored in the dark,
L236@P4: at room temperature for 24 hours, or at refrigerator temperatures for 1 week with minimal loss of potency and clarity. Any unused
L237@P4: material should then be discarded. Solutions prepared for intravenous infusion (0.1 mg or less amphotericin B per mL) should be used
L238@P4: promptly after preparation and should be protected from light during administration.
